cls: Anticoagulant - direct thrombin inhibitor (synthetic hirudin analogue)
quick: PCI: 0.75 mg/kg IV bolus, then 1.75 mg/kg/h infusion for the procedure
No human data; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in milk; caution
Reduce infusion to 1 mg/kg/h if CrCl <30 mL/min; monitor; no bolus change
No dose adjustment expected (not hepatically metabolized)
No direct interaction; relevant only to bleeding risk
ACT (5 min after bolus); signs of bleeding; hemoglobin/hematocrit
summary: Bivalirudin is a synthetic, reversible direct thrombin inhibitor used as an anticoagulant in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), including those with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT/HITTS). Given as an IV bolus plus infusion, it has a short half-life and a predictable, reversible effect. The principal risk is bleeding. It has been studied only with concomitant aspirin.
indications: Anticoagulation in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
PCI in patients with, or at risk of, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and HIT with thrombosis syndrome (HITTS)

dosage.d: 0.75 mg/kg IV bolus, then 1.75 mg/kg/h IV infusion
dosage.t: Bolus then continuous infusion for duration of PCI
dosage.n: Given with aspirin; consider extending infusion up to 4 h in STEMI

dosage.d: Additional 0.3 mg/kg IV bolus if needed
dosage.t: If ACT inadequate 5 min after first bolus

dosage.d: Bolus unchanged 0.75 mg/kg; reduce infusion to 1 mg/kg/h
dosage.n: Monitor ACT; dialysis patients clear ~25% by HD

admin: Reconstitute and dilute per labeling (in 5% dextrose or 0.9% sodium chloride) to 0.5 or 5 mg/mL
Administer the bolus IV, then begin the weight-based infusion immediately
Always given with aspirin; with or without a P2Y12 inhibitor per protocol
Check an activated clotting time (ACT) 5 minutes after the bolus and give a supplemental bolus if needed
Discard unused reconstituted solution; do not mix with other drugs of incompatible pH
moa: Bivalirudin is a specific, reversible direct thrombin inhibitor. It binds both the catalytic active site and the anion-binding exosite of fluid-phase and clot-bound thrombin, inhibiting thrombin-mediated conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, activation of factors V, VIII and XIII, and thrombin-induced platelet activation. Inhibition is transient because thrombin slowly cleaves the bivalirudin molecule, restoring thrombin activity.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to bivalirudin or its components
relative: Severe renal impairment (reduce infusion, increased bleeding risk)
Recent surgery/trauma, bleeding diathesis, severe hypertension

preg: There are no adequate human data. Animal reproduction studies at up to several times the human dose revealed no fetal harm, but risk cannot be excluded. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether bivalirudin is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution; consider the short half-life and the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Clearance is reduced in renal impairment. No change to the bolus, but reduce the infusion to 1 mg/kg/h when CrCl is below 30 mL/min and monitor ACT closely. Approximately 25% is removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is expected; bivalirudin is not metabolized by hepatic enzymes (cleared by proteolysis and renal mechanisms).

major: Other anticoagulants (heparin, warfarin, DOACs, thrombolytics) - additive bleeding risk; avoid overlap
GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors and combined antiplatelet therapy - increased bleeding
moderate: Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors) - intended combination but additive bleeding risk
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; heavy use adds bleeding/GI risk
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs ACT, aPTT, PT/INR and thrombin time; INR not reliable for monitoring

serious: Acute stent thrombosis (notably in primary PCI for STEMI)
rare: Coronary artery thrombosis during diagnostic angiography without anticoagulant continuation
emergency: Acute stent thrombosis / abrupt vessel closure

monitoring: Activated clotting time (ACT) 5 min after bolus during PCI
Clinical signs of bleeding and access site assessment
counsel: This blood thinner is given during your cardiac (angioplasty) procedure to prevent clots
The main risk is bleeding - report any unusual bruising, bleeding, black stools, or blood in urine
Tell the team about any other blood thinners, recent surgery, or bleeding problems
Pressure may be applied at the catheter site afterward to prevent bleeding
pk: Immediate anticoagulant effect after IV bolus
Steady-state plasma concentration within minutes of starting infusion
About 25 minutes in patients with normal renal function (longer in renal impairment)
Short - coagulation parameters return toward baseline ~1 hour after stopping infusion
Store lyophilized vials at 20-25 C (controlled room temperature); reconstituted/diluted solutions per label, refrigerate up to 24 h
pearls: Preferred anticoagulant for PCI in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT/HITTS)
Predictable, reversible effect with short half-life - no routine reversal agent needed; effect dissipates in ~1 hour
In primary PCI for STEMI there is a small increase in early (acute) stent thrombosis - a post-PCI infusion may mitigate this
Only studied with concomitant aspirin; INR is not a valid monitoring test
missed: Not applicable - administered as a single procedural bolus and infusion in a monitored setting, not as scheduled maintenance dosing.
overdose: Overdose (often from failure to reduce the infusion in renal dysfunction) increases the risk of bleeding, including fatal hemorrhage. There is no specific antidote. Discontinue immediately, monitor closely for bleeding, and provide supportive care; approximately 25% is removed by hemodialysis. Use blood products/transfusion as needed for serious bleeding.
